issues.t: Head gasket leaks
issues.sym: Oil or coolant seeping from where the cylinder heads meet the engine block, a sweet coolant or burning oil smell, the coolant tank running low, or the temperature gauge creeping up.
issues.why: The non-turbo 2.5L boxer engine in the Baja shares the head gasket weakness of other Subarus from this era. The gaskets usually start with slow external leaks and can get worse if the engine overheats.
issues.next: Have the leak found and watch the coolant level closely. Fix it before it overheats; many shops do the timing belt and water pump at the same time.

issues.t: Passenger airbag inflator can rupture (recall)
issues.sym: No warning sign. In a crash the passenger airbag inflator can burst and throw metal fragments.
issues.why: The Baja uses a Takata passenger airbag inflator whose propellant breaks down with heat and humidity over the years. Subaru has recalled every Baja model year in several rounds.
issues.next: Check your VIN with a Subaru dealer or NHTSA right away and get the free inflator replacement. Until then, avoid using the front passenger seat.

issues.t: Engine knock or rod bearing failure
issues.sym: A deep knock from the engine that gets louder with revs, low oil pressure light, or the engine seizing.
issues.why: Owners report spun rod bearings and blown engines on both engines, often after running low on oil or overheating.
issues.next: Check the oil level often and stop driving if a knock starts. A worn bearing usually means a replacement or rebuilt engine.

issues.t: Turbo oil screen clogs, causing rough idle or turbo failure
issues.sym: Rough idle, slow rev response, a check engine light for the cam timing, or the turbo whining, smoking or failing.
issues.why: Small mesh filters in the oil banjo bolts feeding the variable cam timing and the turbo can clog with sludge. Subaru issued a bulletin for the damaged filter. Starving the turbo of oil wears it out.
issues.next: Change the oil on time with the right grade. If the idle is rough, have the oil screens checked before the turbo is damaged.

issues.t: AWD binding in tight turns
issues.sym: The truck hops, shudders or feels like it is braking in tight, slow turns such as parking lots, and tires scrub.
issues.why: On automatics, the transfer clutch that splits power front to rear can bind; Subaru issued a bulletin on transfer clutch binding. On manuals, the center differential's viscous coupling can lock up. Mismatched tire sizes make both worse.
issues.next: Make sure all four tires are the same size and evenly worn. Then have the AWD system diagnosed; the automatic's transfer solenoid or clutch is the usual repair.

issues.t: Fuel pump hose connection can crack and leak (recall)
issues.sym: A strong fuel smell, especially after filling up, or fuel dripping near the rear of the vehicle.
issues.why: Cracks can form at the hose connection on the high-pressure side of the fuel pump, letting fuel leak. Subaru recalled 2005-2006 Bajas.
issues.next: Don't drive with a fuel smell. Ask a Subaru dealer to check your VIN for the free fuel pump repair.

issues.t: Overheating from radiator or hose leaks
issues.sym: The temperature gauge climbs, coolant drips under the front, or steam comes from under the hood.
issues.why: Radiators and coolant hoses crack with age. Owners report overheating severe enough to crack the engine block, and overheating also hastens head gasket failure.
issues.next: Stop and shut the engine off if it overheats. Replace a leaking radiator or hose right away rather than topping up.

issues.t: Water pump pulley can come off (recall)
issues.sym: Sudden overheating, a squeal or clatter from the front of the engine, and possibly the engine seizing.
issues.why: The center hole of the water pump pulley was machined wrong on some early vehicles, so the pulley could come loose and stop coolant from flowing.
issues.next: Ask a Subaru dealer to check your VIN for this 2002 recall.

issues.t: Automatic may not hold in Park (recall)
issues.sym: The vehicle can roll after being put in Park.
issues.why: A transmission parking rod was made incorrectly, so Park might not lock the transmission.
issues.next: Always use the parking brake, and ask a Subaru dealer to check your VIN for the free parking rod repair.

issues.t: Oil control valve cover bolts can loosen and leak (recall)
issues.sym: Oil leaking from the front of the engine, a burning oil smell, or smoke from under the hood.
issues.why: Bolts on the cover for the cam timing oil control valve may not have been tightened enough at the factory. Leaking oil can reach hot parts and in rare cases start a fire.
issues.next: Check your VIN with a Subaru dealer for the free bolt fix, and have any oil leak near hot exhaust parts fixed promptly.

issues.t: Automatic transmission fluid leak near the oil filter
issues.sym: Red fluid on the engine near the oil filter or drips under the middle of the vehicle.
issues.why: The automatic can leak fluid at a transmission stud next to the engine's oil filter.
issues.next: Check the transmission fluid level and have the leak sealed. Running the automatic low on fluid can damage it.

issues.t: Torn CV boots and clicking axles
issues.sym: Clicking or tapping when turning, or grease sprayed inside the wheel.
issues.why: The rubber boots on the axles split, the grease escapes and the joints wear. Owners report tapping in turns even after axle replacement, sometimes from cheap aftermarket axles.
issues.next: Replace a torn boot early. If the joint already clicks, replace the axle with a quality part.

issues.t: Wheel bearing hum
issues.sym: A hum or growl that gets louder with speed and may change in turns.
issues.why: Front and rear wheel bearings wear out on these vehicles.
issues.next: Have the bearings checked and replace the noisy one before it gets loose.

issues.t: Rusty or sticking rear brakes
issues.sym: Grinding, pulsing, a pull to one side, or a hot wheel after driving.
issues.why: Owners report pitted, rusted rear rotors early on and sticking rear calipers, especially where roads are salted.
issues.next: Have the rear brakes inspected and the caliper slides cleaned and greased when pads are changed.

issues.t: Clutch release bearing noise
issues.sym: A chirp, squeal or whir with a manual transmission that changes when you press the clutch.
issues.why: Subaru changed the clutch release (throw-out) bearing to use a more heat-resistant grease after noise complaints.
issues.next: If you're replacing the clutch, ask for the updated release bearing.

issues.t: Fuel smell in cold weather
issues.sym: A strong gas smell at startup or when it is below about 30°F.
issues.why: Owners report that rubber fuel hoses under the hood harden in the cold and seep fuel.
issues.next: Have the fuel hoses and clamps checked, and check that the fuel pump recall was done.

issues.t: Valve cover and rear main seal oil leaks
issues.sym: Oil spots under the vehicle, oil on the exhaust, or a burning oil smell.
issues.why: The valve cover gaskets, oil pan seal and rear main seal harden with age and leak.
issues.next: Clean the engine and find the source. Valve cover gaskets are a simple fix; a rear main seal is often done with a clutch job.

issues.t: Rough idle and check engine light after battery disconnect
issues.sym: After the battery is replaced or disconnected, the engine idles roughly and the check engine light may come on.
issues.why: The engine computer loses its learned idle settings. Subaru issued a bulletin describing this and the relearn procedure.
issues.next: Ask a shop to run the idle relearn procedure. It usually settles after normal driving.

issues.t: Rattling exhaust heat shields
issues.sym: A tinny rattle from under the vehicle at certain engine speeds.
issues.why: Heat shield clamps rust and loosen.
issues.next: Have the shields re-secured with new clamps.

issues.t: A/C stops cooling from hose leaks
issues.sym: The A/C blows warm, sometimes after a recharge that didn't last.
issues.why: Owners report cracked A/C hoses and leaking service valves.
issues.next: Have a leak test done before recharging.

issues.t: Steering wheel shake at highway speed
issues.sym: The steering wheel vibrates at highway speeds.
issues.why: Subaru issued a bulletin tracing this to improper wheel balancing.
issues.next: Ask a tire shop for a road-force balance before replacing parts.
